input.quote: Licenses. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, RevMed hereby grants to Sanofi an exclusive (even as to RevMed and its Affiliates), royalty-bearing license (which shall be sub-licensable solely as provided in Section 3.4) under the RevMed Licensed Technology, to Research, Develop, Manufacture, use, sell, offer for sale, import and otherwise Commercialize and exploit Products
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation burdening Sanofi (our client). Full-text passes for "most favored/favoured nation", "no less favorable", "at least as favorable", "more favorable", "MFN", "best terms/price", "match", "right of first negotiation/refusal" and a regex sweep for favo(u)?r returned no MFN mechanic; the only "no less" hits (p0225, p0227, p0244, p0453, p0473) are meeting-frequency, notice-period and confidentiality-care standards. The core grant and economics run the other way: RevMed grants Sanofi an exclusive licence and Sanofi controls pricing and reimbursement approvals (§8.4), with no obligation for Sanofi to extend RevMed terms given to any Third Party and no disclosure or right-to-match mechanic. This meets the preferred position (no Customer MFN obligation), so no redline is proposed; any MFN running in Sanofi's favour would in any event be welcome.
